Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. Each package holds one file, the frontend Go program /usr/bin/build. runtime.main is found in the function table of every Go program scanned, so the tables were read. The build information of the frontend program lists github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 v2.2.0 through v2.3.7 across the builds, but the vulnerable code is not linked in. In every build, the only containerd packages in its function table are core/remotes/docker, core/remotes/docker/auth, core/remotes/errors, internal/lazyregexp, pkg/identifiers, pkg/reference and version (all under github.com/containerd/containerd/v2), and no function table of any Go program in any build contains a function from containerd's pkg/oci package. The fix bounds the user-database reads in containerd's OCI spec options: on release/2.3, commit ff1d116ef9c2d7505306d7d367ef46ff0756460b changes openUserFile in pkg/oci/spec_opts.go; on release/1.7, commit 9ab2b7a894d15738f8323f69def272c29277b57f changes WithAppendAdditionalGroups, UserFromPath, GIDFromPath and getSupplementalGroupsFromPath in oci/spec_opts.go. Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5475, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/ff1d116ef9c2d7505306d7d367ef46ff0756460b, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/9ab2b7a894d15738f8323f69def272c29277b57f . We checked every published trivy package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the repository index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read its Go build information (go version -m) and its function table (go tool nm), and searched its raw bytes, which also finds the names of inlined functions. The Go build information lists github.com/containerd/containerd 1.7.29 to 1.7.32 in builds before 0.71.0-r0, and github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 2.2.0 to 2.2.4 before 0.71.0-r0 and 2.3.1 in 0.71.0-r0 and 0.71.0-r1, inside the affected ranges; from 0.71.2-r0 on the builds carry containerd/v2 2.3.2 to 2.3.7 and no 1.x module. trivy links containerd's client and image packages, but in every build the function table has no user or group function of containerd's OCI spec package (oci or pkg/oci): openUserFile, WithUser, WithUsername, WithAdditionalGIDs, WithAppendAdditionalGroups, UserFromPath, GIDFromPath, UserFromFS, GIDFromFS and getSupplementalGroupsFromPath are absent. Before 0.74.0-r8 no pkg/oci function has its own function-table entry; from 0.74.0-r8 on only its CPU helpers appendCPUThrottlePaths, possibleCPUs and parsePossibleCPUs and its package initializers do. The user-database parser it calls, github.com/moby/sys/user, is present only as its package initializer user.init, while runtime.main is. The raw-byte search of every build finds, under containerd's OCI package, only the inlined descriptor converters DescriptorFromProto and DescriptorToProto, the CPU helpers and initializers above, and the source paths of pkg/oci/spec.go and spec_linux.go; it finds no source path for spec_opts.go, where the user-database code lives, and no openUserFile, openBoundedUserFile, getSupplementalGroupsFromPath, user.ParseGroup or user.ParsePasswd string. The control programs were built with Go 1.27.1, CGO_ENABLED=0, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The vulnerable code is not in the shipped binary.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-47262 (GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq, GO-2026-5475): containerd read an image's /etc/passwd and /etc/group without a size limit when resolving the user and groups of a new container, so a crafted image could exhaust the memory of the containerd process. It affects github.com/containerd/containerd 1.7.0 before 1.7.33 and github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 before 2.0.10, 2.1.9, 2.2.5 and 2.3.2 on those branches. The 1.7.33 and 2.2.5 releases, which list this CVE, bound those reads in the user and group lookups of containerd's OCI spec options (UserFromPath, GIDFromPath, getSupplementalGroupsFromPath and WithAppendAdditionalGroups in 1.7.33; openUserFile, which UserFromFS, GIDFromFS, getSupplementalGroupsFromFS and WithAppendAdditionalGroups use, in 2.2.5): https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/9ab2b7a894d15738f8323f69def272c29277b57f (oci/spec_opts.go, 1.7.33) and https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/30708e8d1142287e9c6bb839f1b3f84c71ca4485 (pkg/oci/spec_opts.go, 2.2.5). Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5475, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v1.7.33 and https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.2.5. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer-dev package published for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository as of 28 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on amd64 and arm64 (50 packages). Each package holds one file, /sbom-indexer, a statically linked Go program for Linux built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter, no dynamic section and no shared-library dependencies). The MD5 checksum each package records for it in the md5sums manifest of its control archive equals that of the program we read in full from the Alpine 3.23 package of the same version and architecture with the matching revision (for example 1.20.4-5 matches 1.20.4-r5 and 1.21.0-0 matches 1.21.0-r0; 1.26.0-3 matches the 1.26.0-r2 program, which 1.26.0-r3 also carries). The -dev program carries the same Go release and module versions as the scout-sbom-indexer program of the same version (it is built without the -w linker flag and without -trimpath). Its Go build information lists github.com/containerd/containerd: v1.7.30 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.20.4-4, v1.7.32 in 1.20.4-5 to 1.21.0-3, v1.7.33 in 1.23.1-0 to 1.23.1-8, v1.7.33 replaced by v1.7.36 in 1.23.1-9 to 1.23.1-10 and not listed in 1.26.0-1 to 1.30.0-0; and github.com/containerd/containerd/v2: v2.2.1 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.20.4-4, v2.2.4 in 1.20.4-5 to 1.21.0-3, v2.2.5 in 1.23.1-0 to 1.23.1-6, v2.3.5 in 1.23.1-8, v2.3.6 in 1.23.1-9 to 1.23.1-10 and v2.4.1 in 1.26.0-1 to 1.30.0-0, the same on both architectures. Reading the program's Go function table in every build (runtime.main found in every build as a control) shows no function of containerd's 1.x oci package; containerd/v2's pkg/oci is linked only in the builds that carry containerd/v2 2.3.6 or 2.4.1, and only for its CPU helpers (parsePossibleCPUs, possibleCPUs, appendCPUThrottlePaths and its initializers). A byte search of every build, which also finds the names of functions the compiler inlined and of closures named after their function, finds none of UserFromPath, UserFromFS, GIDFromPath, GIDFromFS, getSupplementalGroupsFromPath, getSupplementalGroupsFromFS, WithAppendAdditionalGroups, WithAdditionalGIDs, oci.WithUser or openUserFile. So the user and group file reading that the fix bounds is not present in any build, whichever containerd version it carries. As positive controls, the same byte search finds containerd/v2/pkg/oci.parsePossibleCPUs in the builds whose function table lists it, and a test program built with Go 1.27.1, CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath and -ldflags=-w for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against containerd 1.7.30 that calls UserFromPath, GIDFromPath, WithAdditionalGIDs and WithAppendAdditionalGroups links oci.UserFromPath, oci.GIDFromPath, oci.getSupplementalGroupsFromPath and closures named after WithAdditionalGIDs and WithAppendAdditionalGroups, and the byte search finds each of those names in it. The CVE is open in Debian 13 for its containerd package; this decision rests on the code in these builds, not on that status.

The 1.7.33 and 2.2.5 releases, which list this CVE, bound those reads in the user and group lookups of containerd's OCI spec options (UserFromPath, GIDFromPath, getSupplementalGroupsFromPath and WithAppendAdditionalGroups in 1.7.33; openUserFile, which UserFromFS, GIDFromFS, getSupplementalGroupsFromFS and WithAppendAdditionalGroups use, in 2.2.5): https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/9ab2b7a894d15738f8323f69def272c29277b57f (oci/spec_opts.go, 1.7.33) and https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/30708e8d1142287e9c6bb839f1b3f84c71ca4485 (pkg/oci/spec_opts.go, 2.2.5). Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5475, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v1.7.33 and https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.2.5. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer-oci-config package published for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository as of 28 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on amd64 and arm64 (50 packages). Each package holds a single file, /opt/docker/config/scout-sbom-indexer.yaml, a 180-byte YAML configuration file identical in every build (MD5 b0fbc5e6a050e9df1785d32948dade0a in each package's checksum list). The package contains no program, library or archive, so containerd is not present in it. The sbom-indexer program ships in the scout-sbom-indexer and scout-sbom-indexer-dev packages, which are decided separately in this assessment.

CVE-2026-47262 (GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq, GO-2026-5475): containerd read an image's /etc/passwd and /etc/group without a size limit when resolving the user and groups of a new container, so a crafted image could exhaust the memory of the containerd process. It affects github.com/containerd/containerd 1.7.0 before 1.7.33 and github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 before 2.0.10, 2.1.9, 2.2.5 and 2.3.2 on those branches. The 1.7.33 and 2.2.5 releases, which list this CVE, bound those reads in the user and group lookups of containerd's OCI spec options (UserFromPath, GIDFromPath, getSupplementalGroupsFromPath and WithAppendAdditionalGroups in 1.7.33; openUserFile, which UserFromFS, GIDFromFS, getSupplementalGroupsFromFS and WithAppendAdditionalGroups use, in 2.2.5): https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/9ab2b7a894d15738f8323f69def272c29277b57f (oci/spec_opts.go, 1.7.33) and https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/30708e8d1142287e9c6bb839f1b3f84c71ca4485 (pkg/oci/spec_opts.go, 2.2.5). Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5475, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v1.7.33 and https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.2.5. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer package published for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository as of 28 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on amd64 and arm64 (50 packages). Each package holds one file, /sbom-indexer, a statically linked Go program for Linux built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter, no dynamic section and no shared-library dependencies). The MD5 checksum each package records for it in the md5sums manifest of its control archive equals that of the program we read in full from the Alpine 3.23 package of the same version and architecture with the matching revision (for example 1.20.4-5 matches 1.20.4-r5 and 1.21.0-0 matches 1.21.0-r0; 1.26.0-3 matches the 1.26.0-r2 program, which 1.26.0-r3 also carries). The scout-sbom-indexer-dev and scout-sbom-indexer-oci-config packages built from the same source publish the same versions; the -dev program carries the same Go release and module versions as the scout-sbom-indexer program of the same version (it is built without the -w linker flag and without -trimpath), and the -oci-config package holds only a YAML configuration file. Its Go build information lists github.com/containerd/containerd: v1.7.30 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.20.4-4, v1.7.32 in 1.20.4-5 to 1.21.0-3, v1.7.33 in 1.23.1-0 to 1.23.1-8, v1.7.33 replaced by v1.7.36 in 1.23.1-9 to 1.23.1-10 and not listed in 1.26.0-1 to 1.30.0-0; and github.com/containerd/containerd/v2: v2.2.1 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.20.4-4, v2.2.4 in 1.20.4-5 to 1.21.0-3, v2.2.5 in 1.23.1-0 to 1.23.1-6, v2.3.5 in 1.23.1-8, v2.3.6 in 1.23.1-9 to 1.23.1-10 and v2.4.1 in 1.26.0-1 to 1.30.0-0, the same on both architectures. Reading the program's Go function table in every build (runtime.main found in every build as a control) shows no function of containerd's 1.x oci package; containerd/v2's pkg/oci is linked only in the builds that carry containerd/v2 2.3.6 or 2.4.1, and only for its CPU helpers (parsePossibleCPUs, possibleCPUs, appendCPUThrottlePaths and its initializers). A byte search of every build, which also finds the names of functions the compiler inlined and of closures named after their function, finds none of UserFromPath, UserFromFS, GIDFromPath, GIDFromFS, getSupplementalGroupsFromPath, getSupplementalGroupsFromFS, WithAppendAdditionalGroups, WithAdditionalGIDs, oci.WithUser or openUserFile. So the user and group file reading that the fix bounds is not present in any build, whichever containerd version it carries. As positive controls, the same byte search finds containerd/v2/pkg/oci.parsePossibleCPUs in the builds whose function table lists it, and a test program built with Go 1.27.1, CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath and -ldflags=-w for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against containerd 1.7.30 that calls UserFromPath, GIDFromPath, WithAdditionalGIDs and WithAppendAdditionalGroups links oci.UserFromPath, oci.GIDFromPath, oci.getSupplementalGroupsFromPath and closures named after WithAdditionalGIDs and WithAppendAdditionalGroups, and the byte search finds each of those names in it. The CVE is open in Debian 13 for its containerd package; this decision rests on the code in these builds, not on that status.
